claim: In pulse interrupt mode the acknowledge cycle reads FF from the bus, so IM 2 takes its handler address from I x 256 + FF and IM 0 behaves as IM 1; a device on an enabled expansion bus can put its own byte there.
limit: Measured on a KS1 (core 3.03.00, nxsuite I01), no expansion-bus device; other cores not measured. docs/BRIEFING.md lists it as relied on.

evidence.source: I. Novak, Unraveling the ZX Spectrum Next, Vol 1 (2026; core 3.03.03), chapter 4
evidence.text: The FPGA drives FF itself in pulse mode. In hardware IM2 mode (NextREG 0xC0 bit 0) the vector is 0xC0 bits 7-5, then a 4-bit source number, then 0: line 0, CTC 0-3 are 3-6, ULA 11.
KS1 Issue 2, core 3.03.00 (nxsuite I01): in pulse mode IM 2 took its handler address from I x 256 + $FF.
